prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper) coordinates incidents, dispatch, jurisdictional coverage, shared records, surge and mutual aid; jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local-policy responsibility. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur) confirms/repeats location, collects callback, symptoms/onset/access details and pediatric age, available weight and caregiver observations; preserves original reports, separates facts/estimates, produces Caller Location Correction Slip and receives Bedside Arrival Receipt, verifying arrival time. Triage requires reassessment; pediatric airway, breathing, circulation or mental-status concerns get prompt approved-protocol escalation. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield) resolves uncertainty, records priority/rationale/response level, sends Pediatric Acuity Note, validates surge and approves/documents temporary triage overrides before use; reviews audit memo before closing suspected duplicate incidents. Regional Medical Director sets clinical policy/priorities, advises specialty care/destinations and guides non-routine demand/protocol adjustments; no dispatch authority. Shift Commander (Sundial) manages readiness/surge/coverage, reviews coverage before moves, approves material coverage-reducing exceptions, sends Mutual Aid Release Form on neighboring-service release, reviews access/transfer issues and ensures assignments, destination constraints and staffing gaps hand over after surge. Paramedic Crew reports readiness/status, position, changes and route hazards; remains staged until relocation/direct assignment confirmed, reassesses pediatric patients en route and reports material changes to receiving facility. Ambulance Unit 417 reports arrival/handover and may be reassigned only after dispatch confirms obligations permit. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) manages Regional Radio Network reachability/backups, assignments, priority/routes and Coverage Gap Bulletin below threshold. Network carries dispatch/crew and mutual-aid traffic using agreed call signs; crews acknowledge/repeat critical location, priority and destination; retry unacknowledged calls, correct discrepancies with fresh transmission; handoff requires acknowledgment/dispatch confirmation. Degraded-radio mode prioritizes emergency traffic/common operating picture; operators announce outages, affected areas/restoration, and Mistral directs approved fallback channels, acknowledged/repeated before movement. North/South Gate Status Boards show respective access conditions; South produces South Access Lane Notice. Ambulance Coordination Platform time-stamps changes and separates accepted mutual-aid resources from local units. Fleet Maintenance Cell reports restrictions promptly. Kestrel (Hospital Liaison Desk) confirms capacity/pediatric limitations before destination finalization, records facility responses/constraints and informs dispatch; Riverside Trauma Center advises Kestrel of trauma-intake suitability constraints. Emergency Department acknowledges destination changes and access restrictions. Data Quality

Document units:
S202: If voice contact fails, dispatchers use the approved data channel when available and record the time of each attempted contact.
S203: Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays the latest confirmed unit status alongside the time and source of that confirmation.
S204: Ambulance Coordination Platform preserves queued status updates during brief connection interruptions and flags records that require reconciliation.
S205: Coverage monitoring compares successful radio checks with the planned check interval for each operating area.
S206: North Gate Status Board and South Gate Status Board provide separate views of access conditions that may affect radio reach or ambulance movement.
S207: Radio Coordinator uses the change card to adjust channel assignments and record the effective time of each change.
S208: Shift Commander receives the Coverage Gap Bulletin and decides whether staffing or deployment adjustments are needed.
S209: Data Quality Officer reviews Pebble for conflicting timestamps before interrupted communications are reconciled.
S210: Triage Supervisor identifies calls whose clinical priority requires immediate radio access and communicates that priority to dispatch staff.
S211: Call Taker Mara keeps the caller connected when feasible while dispatch staff attempt to reach the assigned crew through an approved alternate channel.
S212: Ambulance Unit 417 reports its last confirmed position and safe operating status as soon as contact is restored.
S213: Fleet Maintenance Cell reports radio equipment faults through the established maintenance escalation path.
S214: Hospital Liaison Desk uses available telephone channels to confirm whether receiving facilities can accept arrivals during a network disruption.
S215: Emergency Department staff receive concise arrival updates through the approved backup contact method when radio delivery is unavailable.
S216: Regional Medical Director may advise on clinical prioritization when communication limits materially affect response choices.
S217: Paramedic Crew members follow local safety procedures and do not enter an area where dispatch instructions cannot be confirmed if conditions are uncertain.
S218: Shift Commander retains operational authority until a named successor acknowledges the handover or a higher-level incident command arrangement takes effect.
S219: The outgoing shift records active incidents, communication failures, temporary channel assignments, and decisions awaiting review.
S220: The incoming shift verifies open assignments and confirms which communication paths remain available before accepting control.
S221: After service is restored, dispatch staff reconcile delayed status reports against their recorded timestamps and preserve any unresolved discrepancy for review.
S222: The Regional Dispatch Center maintains controlled procedures for reviewing operational records, approving system changes, and documenting corrective actions.
S223: The Data Quality Officer samples incident records for completeness, timestamp consistency, and alignment between dispatch decisions and recorded outcomes.
